findings.where: First screen, the contact row: the blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action doesn't work. 'Write to me' looks like a button and the address is underlined like a link, but clicking either does nothing. The parts map shows both as static. The only working mailto link is the small footer address at the very bottom of the page.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to get in touch clicks 'Write to me', nothing happens, and they have to copy the address out by hand. At the moment of intent the site looks broken, and an advisor whose site looks broken loses credibility.

findings.where: First screen, the 'Book a consultation' button next to 'Write to me'
findings.fault: The first screen has a second, competing call to action, where the brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach him. 'Book a consultation' is a sales-funnel phrase from a firm, and it points to #consult, a section the page doesn't have. It promises a booking system that a brochure site with no bespoke software won't have.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one action and fails anything salesy or firm-like. Mark, who hasn't offered bookable consultations. The visitor, who has to choose between two buttons and then finds the second one goes nowhere.

findings.where: First screen, the three blue margin notes (Istanbul 2025, Melbourne 2026, São Paulo 2024)
findings.fault: His strongest proof, dated talks at named venues, is in link blue but can't be clicked. The parts map shows all three as static. A reader can't open the talk or its slides to check the claim.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader who judges standing by checkable work. They click a talk title expecting the talk, get nothing, and the proof looks like decoration.

findings.where: First screen, the uppercase first-person paragraph ('I advise multilateral development banks, development agencies and governments…')
findings.fault: His standing is only claimed by category. No named bank, agency, government, role or country of his advisory work appears, and no third-party proof appears anywhere on the page. The only named body is the university he lectures at. Nothing shows 'who asked me' (for example, 'The Asian Development Bank asked me to prepare…').
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff who select individual consultants against terms of reference. They have to be sure he has done this kind of work for bodies like theirs, in their region, and this first screen doesn't show it.

findings.where: Header navigation (Profile, Articles and Presentations, Blog) and the whole page
findings.fault: The navigation has no 'Contact' item, and the page never says where Mark is based. The margin notes give the places of his talks, not his base country or the regions where he has advised.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who arrives on any page other than this first screen has no labelled route to Mark. A bank officer checking eligibility or time zone has no base to go on.

findings.where: Phone, the hero: the contact row
findings.fault: On a phone, the way to reach Mark comes only after the heading, a margin note, the full photograph, the uppercase paragraph, a second note, the second paragraph and a third note, roughly three screens down. The first phone screen has no way to reach him.
findings.who_objects: A reader who arrives from a LinkedIn post on their phone and wants to write has to scroll past all the hero content to find out how.
